decisions.statement: One ask answers a closure whichever way its predicate follows an edge.
Which edges are followed and which way is read off the predicate handed in.
The seeds a closure starts from are handed to the ask.
A seed the ask takes in is part of the closure the ask answers.
Which nodes a closure takes in is handed to the ask.
An ask taking in every node it reaches says so by handing in no gate.
A predicate followed out of a file is answered from a reader of file bodies.
A predicate followed into a file reads no body.
An ask handing in no reader is refused where its predicate is followed out.
A node already in the closure is stepped from once.
A file no edge is read out of is still part of the closure that reached it.
The closure comes back sorted, so two asks alike answer alike.
No caller names an edge kind or a direction of its own.
Nothing here reads an edge, which the graph is asked for.
An ask answers the edges a closure took in as well as the nodes.
An edge reaching a node already taken in is answered, so a closure shows its cycles.
An edge the gate refuses the far end of is no part of the closure.
An ask wanting only the nodes is answered only those.
A predicate following an attribute value takes in only an edge carrying that value.
An edge a predicate does not follow leaves the node beyond that edge unreached.
An edge carrying none of an attribute a predicate follows is refused rather than dropped.

definition: the closure a predicate takes in from the seeds it is handed
